facts.text: Leggett officially became a town on February 15 1895, when the North Carolina General Assembly defined its boundaries around the old Leggett residence and Presbyterian church.
Mount Prospect, an 18th‑century Georgian plantation house built between 1772 and 1796, still stands in Leggett and earned a spot on the National Register of Historic Places.
Cedar Lane, the Fountain House, is a late‑1840s Greek Revival home with a double‑pile plan and hip roof, and it is listed on the National Register.
Before Europeans arrived, the Tuscarora people inhabited the area that would become Leggett, leaving a legacy that echoes in the town’s early history.
Edgecombe County, where Leggett sits, was formed in 1741 from Bertie County and named after English politician Baron Richard Edgecombe.
Leggett is part of the Rocky Mount Metropolitan Statistical Area, linking it to a larger regional community.
